column1: # enforces (DND-218). One line per first-party file: path<TAB>class<TAB>reason.
# A guard needs no reason, so `path<TAB>guard` and `path<TAB>guard<TAB>` parse
# the same. An editor that strips a guard row's trailing tab changes nothing;
# do not repair it. (Measured 2026-10-01: DND-1354 and DND-1479 each re-inserted
# such a row by script after the Edit tool dropped the tab.)
# Classes: guard (must carry Fix:) | tool | no-fail-path | library.
# Every class but guard states the real reason the file has no guard failure
# path. Test suites (a test/ path segment, *.self-test.sh) are classified by
# rule and never listed. Files under ai/hooks and ai/bin are guards unless
# A new executable or lib/ file that is not listed here FAILS the check. That is
# the point: an unclassified script is the drift. Never list a guard as
# anything else to make the gate green; give it a Fix: line instead.
# This table is ratcheted against its LANDED copy (DND-510): a path that is a
# guard on origin/main or at the merge-base cannot become a non-guard in a
# branch. The owner lands a genuine reclassification on main themselves.
# --- ai/hooks and ai/bin default to guard (GUARD_DIRS); only exceptions are listed.
